paper.title: A near-complete Landrace pig (Sus scrofa) genome resolves centromeres and telomeres and highlights telomere repeat structures in different pig breeds.
paper.abstract: The Duroc-derived reference genome Sscrofa11.1 has provided a critical foundation for pig genomics, supporting accurate variant detection and comparative analyses, but does not capture breed-specific variation. Here, we present a near-complete genome assembly for the Landrace pig (Landrace_v1, GCA_963921485.1), spanning all 20 chromosomes and totaling 2.6 Gb, including 176 Mb of sequence absent from Sscrofa11.1. Comparative analyses with recently published high-quality pig genomes reveals conserved centromere organization across breeds, accompanied by substantial variation in repeat composition and length, and identifies a pig-specific pattern of telomere variant repeats across eight breeds. The improved resolution of repetitive regions in Landrace_v1 enables more complete reconstruction of complex gene families, including olfactory receptors, and uncovers structural variation at the KIT proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase locus absent from the Duroc reference. Together, these findings highlight limitations of single-reference genomes and demonstrate the value of breed-specific assemblies for capturing genomic diversity and improving downstream analyses.

paper.title: 'I Just Wanted It to End': Sensory Experiences of Autistic Women During Pregnancy and Childbirth.
paper.abstract: Autistic women experience the perinatal cycle with specific sensory challenges that remain insufficiently documented, particularly among those with diverse support levels. This qualitative study investigated sensory processing experiences of autistic women during pregnancy and labour, and how environmental and attitudinal factors articulate with sensory overload. Thirty-four autistic Brazilian women with Support Levels 1 and 2 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders [5th ed., text rev.]) participated in four Hermeneutic-Dialectic Circle (HDC) cycles through semi-structured interviews in multiple formats. Iterative hermeneutic-dialectic analysis, supported by NVivo, identified four themes: (1) Pregnancy as a sensory amplifier; (2) The birth environment as the epicentre of sensory overload; (3) Communication barriers and professional invalidation; and (4) Sensory experiences in early motherhood. Pregnancy amplified pre-existing sensitivities, particularly olfactory and proprioceptive. The hospital environment emerged as the epicentre of overload, with touch as the most aversive stimulus. Peritraumatic dissociation was reported by 19 participants (56%). The deliberate inclusion of women with intellectual disability and complex communication needs revealed that saturation observed in earlier cycles was artifactual, a finding with methodological implications for qualitative autism research.Lay AbstractAutistic women often face challenges during pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period related to how they process sensory information such as sounds, lights, touch and smells. Very little research has explored how these differences affect the experience of becoming a mother, and even less has included autistic women with higher support needs or complex communication needs. This study explored the sensory experiences of 34 autistic women in Brazil through in-depth interviews, deliberately including women with Support Levels 1 and 2, some of whom used augmentative and alternative communication. The interviews were conducted in multiple formats (video call, in-person and text messaging) to ensure accessibility. We found that pregnancy amplified pre-existing sensory sensitivities. Smells, temperature changes and foetal movement were experienced with an intensity far beyond what is typically reported, sometimes causing shutdowns and crises. The hospital birth environment was a major source of sensory overload, with touch being the most distressing stimulus: 31 of 34 women reported aversive experiences related to being touched during labour. Even comfort techniques widely recommended for pain relief, such as massage, were described as unbearable. Communication barriers intensified suffering throughout the perinatal cycle: women reported that health care professionals frequently dismissed their sensory experiences as exaggeration or anxiety, which made it harder to access appropriate care. More than half the participants (19 of 34) reported memory gaps and dissociation during labour, suggesting that childbirth can be a traumatic event for autistic women when care is not adapted to their sensory needs. When health care teams made accommodations (reducing lighting, minimising unnecessary touch, maintaining continuity of care, providing predictability), women reported substantially better experiences. A key methodological finding was that the apparent saturation of themes observed when only women with Support Level 1 were interviewed proved artifactual: including women with higher support needs revealed new and important experiences that would otherwise have been missed. These findings highlight the need for sensory-informed, neurodiversity-affirming perinatal care and for research that deliberately includes autistic women with diverse support levels and communication profiles.

paper.title: Multimodal Neurorehabilitation Including Auditory EEG Neurofeedback: A Proof of Concept Tested After Resection of a Giant Olfactory Groove Meningioma.
paper.abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients undergoing resection of large olfactory groove meningiomas may present with persistent cognitive, behavioral, motor, and functional impairments. Evidence regarding EEG neurofeedback as part of postoperative neurorehabilitation remains preliminary. This case report describes the feasibility and associated clinical and neurophysiological changes in a sensory-adapted multimodal rehabilitation program. Methods: A 53-year-old man underwent emergency resection of a giant olfactory groove meningioma and subsequently completed 20 inpatient rehabilitation sessions over four weeks. Each session included auditory SMR/theta EEG neurofeedback at Cz, individualized cognitive training, and physiotherapy. Neuropsychological, emotional, functional, and mobility outcomes were assessed before and after treatment. EEG outcomes included longitudinal single-channel recordings acquired during neurofeedback sessions and 19-channel resting-state recordings obtained under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions before and after the program. Spectral power, spectral ratios, and weighted phase-lag index connectivity were analyzed descriptively. Results: Reliable or measurement-based improvements were observed in global cognition, executive functioning, immediate and delayed verbal recall, total and cognitive functional independence, and mobility. Across the 20 neurofeedback sessions, the conservative primary analysis retained 9936 of 10,261 epochs and showed reduced theta activity, increased SMR and beta activity, increased SMR/theta, and reduced theta/total-beta. Resting-state EEG showed lower relative theta power and higher SMR, beta-1, and beta-2 power under both recording conditions. Connectivity changes included reduced theta and posterior alpha coupling together with increased SMR connectivity across fronto-central and parieto-occipital networks. Conclusions: Sensory-adapted EEG neurofeedback was feasible within an intensive multimodal rehabilitation program and was accompanied by concurrent cognitive, functional, and neurophysiological changes. Because of the single-case, uncontrolled, multimodal design, the findings cannot establish treatment-specific efficacy and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

paper.title: Volatile Metabolomics Reveals the Effects of Different Bagging Types on Peel Aroma of 'Siam Red Pomelo'.
paper.abstract: Fruit bagging is a common horticultural practice, but its effects on citrus peel volatile metabolism remain poorly understood. Citrus maxima 'Siam Red Pomelo' is a distinctive red-skinned pomelo germplasm, and the influence of different bagging types on its peel volatile composition has not been systematically characterized. In this study, peel volatiles from fruit subjected to a non-bagged control (CK), a white nonwoven bag (W), and a yellow-black double-layer paper bag (B) were profiled using HS-SPME-GC-MS. Relative odor activity values (rOAVs), calculated from single-internal-standard semi-quantitative VOC estimates and literature-reported odor thresholds, were used to prioritize compounds with potential aroma relevance. A total of 1598 volatile organic compounds were identified, mainly terpenoids and esters. The two bagging treatments produced distinct volatile metabolic profiles. The B treatment showed relatively greater contributions of several sesquiterpenoids and oxygenated derivatives, including 7-epi-α-eudesmol and caryophyllene oxide, together with reduced contributions of several green-associated monoterpenes. In contrast, the W treatment showed relatively greater contributions of monoterpene esters, such as linalyl butyrate, associated with database-reported floral and fruity odor descriptors. KEGG enrichment indicated treatment-associated changes in terpenoid biosynthesis and butanoate metabolism. Overall, different bag types were associated with distinct peel volatile profiles and distributions of putative aroma-related compounds. Because the rOAVs were based on semi-quantitative data and no GC-olfactometry, aroma recombination/omission experiments, or sensory evaluation was performed, the inferred aroma-related differences should be regarded as hypotheses requiring sensory validation.

Here, we review and assemble the morphological, proteomic, genomic and behavioural evidence for that unusual selection response at four levels. RJ production may be dominated by a heritable polygenic trait whose acceptance and secretion components carry significant genotypic variance, and the selected candidate genomic architecture combines a large inversion with the tandem mrjp cluster. RJB nurses could detect larval volatiles more sensitively, and cross-fostering suggests that larval acceptance depends on the genotype of the nurse bees, not that of the larvae. RJB hypopharyngeal glands develop larger acini, delayed regression and reinforced protein synthesis, whereas mandibular glands up-regulate the fatty-acid pathway that may yield 10-HDA. An expanded nurse-stage neuropeptidome and a remodelled brain membrane proteome may tune larval recognition, water homeostasis and pollen collection. paper.title: Disruption of Male Spodoptera litura Pheromone Attraction by Structurally Related Compounds: Electrophysiological and Field Evidence.
paper.abstract: The tobacco cutworm, Spodoptera litura, is a globally important agricultural pest that relies on a female-produced sex pheromone blend for mate location. Here, we investigated the electrophysiological and behavioral responses of S. litura to its sex pheromone components and structurally related compounds using gas chromatography-electroantennogrm detection (GC-EAD) and field trapping assays. Most of the 17 compounds tested elicited antennal responses in both sexes, although response magnitude and sensitivity differed markedly among compounds and between males and females. Male responses were generally stronger, but females also detected several pheromone-related compounds with high sensitivity, demonstrating previously unrecognized pheromone autodetection in S. litura. In field assays, four compounds, Z7-12:Ac, Z9-14:Ac, Z9-14:OH, and Z9E12-14:Ac, strongly inhibited male attraction to the conspecific pheromone. Other structurally related compounds either had weaker or inconsistent inhibitory effects. Our findings suggest that broad sensitivity to structurally related and heterospecific pheromone compounds may contribute to discrimination among chemically similar odor signals and thereby facilitate species recognition and reproductive isolation in Spodoptera. The potent behavioral antagonists identified here also provide promising candidates for the development of pheromone-based, environmentally sustainable approaches to S. litura management.

paper.title: Functional Analysis of Odorant-Degrading Enzymes Responding to the Repellent Activity of 2,3-Dimethyl-6-(1-Hydroxy)-Pyrazine Against Plutella xylostella.
paper.abstract: Plutella xylostella is an important cruciferous crop pest with critical resistance to many chemical insecticides; 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine has shown obvious repellent activity against P. xylostella with significant effects on the olfactory system. These findings illustrate that PxylGSTS1 plays an important role in the response to 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine, which can be used in the green control of P. xylostella and other Lepidopteran pests in the field.

paper.title: Identification and Behavioral Evaluation of Ketone Attractants for the Stable Fly, Stomoxys calcitrans.
paper.abstract: The stable fly, Stomoxys calcitrans L., is one of the most damaging blood-feeding pests of livestock. Stable flies use odors associated with vertebrate hosts and their environments to locate blood meal and suitable oviposition and larval-development sites. Previous studies have identified behaviorally active gases, phenolic compounds, short-chain fatty acids, alcohols, and sulfur-containing compounds from cattle-associated odor sources, but ketones have received limited behavioral investigation. We first evaluated stable-fly attraction to host- and resource-associated substrates, including chicken manure, wet blood meal and sheep blood and characterized volatile compounds from attractive materials using SPME-GC-MS. We then tested ketones detected in the headspace of these substrates or reported in published studies. Three ketones, 1-octen-3-one, 3-octanone, and 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one, significantly attracted adult stable flies. Following blend evaluation, 3-octanone and 1-octen-3-one were selected as the two-component K-lure blend which was significantly more attractive than the control in choice assays. Combining K-lure with the previously reported phenol-m-cresol blend elicited the highest response among the treatments tested. In a subsequent sticky-card trapping assay, traps baited with K-lure captured significantly more stable flies than the control traps. These results identify ketones as stable fly attractants and support further evaluation of K-lure in trap-based monitoring and management.

paper.title: Plant-Derived Control of Postprandial Glycemia: α-Amylase, α-Glucosidase, and the Incretin-DPP-4 Interface.
paper.abstract: Postprandial hyperglycemia can be modified before absorbed glucose reaches the circulation. Plant-derived compounds may slow starch hydrolysis through α-amylase and intestinal α-glucosidases, stimulate glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) release, or preserve incretin activity through dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibition. This critical narrative review integrates these mechanisms around intestinal exposure, substrate selectivity, and human evidence. Flavonoids show structure-dependent and time-dependent inhibition of carbohydrate-hydrolyzing enzymes, but results vary markedly between yeast, rodent, and human enzyme systems. Iminosugar-rich mulberry preparations and thiosugar-containing Salacia extracts provide the strongest chemistry-to-clinic examples, including randomized trials that reduced postprandial glucose or HbA1c. Preclinical studies suggest that berberine may link bitter-taste-receptor-mediated GLP-1 secretion with local intestinal DPP-4 effects, whereas mangiferin, flavonol glycosides, anthocyanins, and food-derived peptides remain supported mainly by preclinical studies. In vitro potency alone is insufficient: meal composition, enzyme source, luminal concentration, metabolism, product standardization, gastrointestinal tolerance, and incretin measurements determine translational value. Candidate prioritization requires defined chemistry, achievable exposure, and product-specific human validation; acute effects do not establish durable benefit or human target engagement.

paper.title: MIDAS: Multi-Sensorial Immersive Dynamic Autonomous System for Stroke Hand Rehabilitation-Prototype Design and Exploratory User Evaluation.
paper.abstract: Many stroke survivors experience impaired function in their paretic hands. Maintaining motivation to continue hand rehabilitation exercises can be challenging. Together, these components engage four senses during rehabilitation. A pilot study involving five people affected by stroke was conducted across three sessions. The subsystems of MIDAS were added progressively in each session. The game environment, sound effects, and scent were selected to create a multisensory experience. User experience scores were higher in Session 3 than in Session 1 for four participants and unchanged for one. Stroke Rehabilitation Motivation Scale (SRMS) scores decreased across sessions for two participants, increased between Sessions 1 and 3 for two, and remained unchanged for one. Responses to several individual questionnaire items were favorable, but the study did not establish an overall increase in rehabilitation motivation.

paper.title: Exploratory whole-genome sequencing of cagA-positive Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric biopsies: descriptive observations in COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric disease involves sustained inflammation, stromal responses, and extracellular-matrix remodeling, yet genomic observations shared across different clinical categories remain poorly defined. This study aimed to describe variant-associated gene annotations in four cagA-positive gastric-biopsy specimens with different documented clinical and histological findings, without inferring within-patient progression.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing (2 × 151 bp; approximately 37.7× mean mappable depth) was performed on gastric-biopsy DNA from four unrelated adults with active gastritis, normal histology with positive H. pylori screening assays, gastric ulcer, and intestinal-type adenocarcinoma. Variant-associated gene sets were annotated by KEGG, Reactome, and Gene Ontology over-representation analysis with within-analysis Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction, and term-level outputs were examined for denominator consistency, gene-family representation, and overlapping membership. Across six analysis sets and five annotation collections, 141 BH-significant term occurrences represented 94 distinct database-term pairs. The intersection of significant-term contributors from three principal analysis sets contained 133 genes, including 124 olfactory-receptor genes and nine other genes. COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12 were examined as literature-informed discussion targets. Five of six displayed alleles had global gnomAD-genome frequencies above 20%, whereas ICAM1 rs542476616 was rare globally. No category association was tested.

CONCLUSIONS: The study describes shared genomic annotations in four cagA-positive gastric biopsies and provides a traceable term-level analysis. COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12 motivate further genotype-confirmed and clinically adjudicated investigation; their recurrence does not establish diagnostic performance or a disease-associated variant effect.

paper.title: Post-COVID neurological manifestations are associated with neuroinflammation, increased autoantibody burden, and persistent complement activation.
paper.abstract: Neurological manifestations represent commonly persistent features of post-COVID conditions (PCC), but mechanisms underlying their pathogenesis remain unclear. In this study, participants with neuro-PCC (n = 29), mostly presenting with persistent headache, fatigue, sleep disturbances, anosmia/dysgeusia, cognitive complaints, and/or paresthesia, recovered from COVID-19 (n = 32), and non-infected controls (n = 32), all matched for sex and age, had paired serum samples from acute phase (0-14 days) and two time points of convalescence (3-6 months and 9-12 months) assessed for antinuclear antibodies (ANA), antibodies to extractable nuclear antigens (ENA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), and autoantibodies against cytokines using Luminex assays. Biomarkers of neuroinflammation, including neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), total Tau protein, and neurogranin were quantified by Ella ELISA and complement activation was determined by increased C5b-9 levels. Patients with neuro-PCC showed a greater number of neurological symptoms during acute phase, with increased frequency of headache and fatigue, and a higher prevalence of obesity and cardiovascular comorbidities. GFAP remained elevated for up to one year after infection, independently of symptom persistence. However, only patients with neuro-PCC exhibited a transient increase in NfL levels during acute phase, and persistent complement activation throughout follow-up. No specific autoantibody was associated with neuro-PCC, but these patients exhibited a higher cumulative autoantibody burden. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that hospitalization and the neurological burden during the acute phase were associated with neuro-PCC, whereas anti-cytokine autoantibody counts showed an inverse trend. Increased complement activation and a higher autoantibody burden suggest a broad and nonspecific immune activation that may contribute to a sustained low-grade neuroinflammatory state, potentially driving the persistence of neurological symptoms after COVID-19.

paper.title: Neurotoxicity and mechanism of titanium dioxide nanoparticles.
paper.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO₂ NPs) are widely used, raising concerns about neurotoxicity. This review summarizes their pathways into the central nervous system, brain distribution, and neurotoxic mechanisms. Evidence indicates TiO₂ NPs may reach the brain via the blood-brain barrier, olfactory nerve pathways, and systemic circulation. While titanium is detected in regions like the hippocampus, cortex, and cerebellum, total Ti measurements do not confirm intact nanoparticle translocation. Mechanisms primarily involve oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, neurotransmitter disruption, and protein aggregation, modulated by particle size, phase, coating, and exposure route. Crystal-phase effects are highly cell-type-specific, precluding a fixed anatase/rutile toxicity ranking, and mixed-phase materials may show enhanced photocatalytic ROS generation under specific conditions. We also address current research limitations and risk assessment challenges to support the safe application of TiO₂ NPs.

paper.title: Preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in mice, along with gut microbial and succinate alterations.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder frequently accompanied by gut dysbiosis and neurobehavioral comorbidities, but the microbial metabolites mediating gut-skin crosstalk remain unclear. We investigated whether preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and characterized the accompanying gut microbiome, succinate, intestinal, and behavioral alterations.

METHODS: HEM20-01 was orally administered to NC/Nga mice beginning 2 weeks before house dust mite (HDM) induction and continued throughout the 4-week induction period. Cutaneous and intestinal inflammation were assessed by histology, gene expression, and multiplex cytokine analysis, and behavior by the open field test. Fecal microbiota composition and metabolite profiles were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and gas chromatography-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (GC-TOF-MS)-based metabolomics. Exogenous succinate was administered in an independent MC903-induced dermatitis model to test whether succinate can aggravate these responses.

RESULTS: HDM-induced AD-like mice showed activation of the intestinal succinate receptor 1 (SUCNR1)-tuft cell-IL-25 axis and enrichment of the putative succinate-associated family Rikenellaceae and its genus Alistipes, together with elevated fecal and plasma succinate. Preventive HEM20-01 administration attenuated the development of cutaneous and intestinal inflammatory phenotypes. HEM20-01-treated mice also showed a lower relative abundance of putative succinate-associated taxa (Bacteroidaceae, Rikenellaceae, Christensenellaceae, Bacteroides, and Alistipes), lower circulating succinate levels, reduced activation of SUCNR1-tuft cell-IL-25-related signaling, and attenuated behavioral and hippocampal serotonergic alterations compared with untreated AD-like mice. In a separate MC903-induced dermatitis model, succinate supplementation exacerbated cutaneous and intestinal inflammation.

CONCLUSIONS: Preventive HEM20-01 administration attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and associated behavioral alterations, accompanied by changes in gut microbiome composition, lower circulating succinate, and intestinal inflammatory signaling.

paper.title: Molecular modulation of cholinergic and neuromuscular signaling following long-term acetaminophen administration.
paper.abstract: Acetaminophen is widely used as an analgesic and antipyretic; however, its long-term neurochemical actions remain incompletely characterized. Its bioactive metabolite, N-arachidonoylphenolamine (AM404), activates transient receptor potential vanilloid type 1 (TRPV1) and cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1), both of which are involved in the regulation of cholinergic signaling. Human neural stem cells and mouse myoblast cells were treated with AM404 (0-1.0 μg/mL), and Sprague-Dawley rats received oral acetaminophen (0, 10, 100, or 1000 mg/kg/day) for 4 weeks. In vitro, AM404 increased the expression of TRPV1, CB1, choline transporter (CHT), choline acetyltransferase (ChAT), and vesicular ACh transporter (VAChT) in F3 cells. Meanwhile, it upregulated CHRNA1, ryanodine receptor 1 (RyR1), and sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2⁺-ATPase 1 (SERCA1) in C2C12 cells. In vivo, chronic acetaminophen administration elevated TRPV1, CB1, CHT, ChAT, and VAChT in the brain and sciatic nerve, increased cerebrospinal ACh concentrations, and increased expression of CHRNA1, RyR1, and SERCA1 in skeletal muscle. Hepatotoxicity was observed only at the highest dose (1000 mg/kg), whereas at lower doses molecular changes in cholinergic and neuromuscular-related markers were observed without overt liver injury. These observations provide new insight into the neuromodulatory properties of acetaminophen and warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models.

paper.title: From past to present and toward the future: a mechanism-informed clinical framework for COVID-19-associated headache and post-viral pain.
paper.abstract: Headache is a prominent acute and persistent neurological manifestation of COVID-19, representing both as a significant clinical challenge and a valuable model for understanding the neurotropic effects of SARS-CoV-2. This review synthesizes evidence showing that the epidemiology of COVID-19 headache is distinctly shaped by younger age, female sex, and a prior history of headache disorders; its clinical phenotypes are diverse, strongly associating with chemosensory dysfunctions such as anosmia; and its core pathophysiology involves neuroinflammation (e.g., cytokine-mediated pathways), trigeminovascular activation, and sex-specific neuroendocrine-immune interactions. Although acute headache often responds to conventional analgesics, persistent cases-a major component of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)-necessitate a multidisciplinary management approach. This contrasts with the typically self-limiting headache following vaccination. Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to define chronicity, mechanistic investigations into sex-specific pathways, and the development of phenotype-specific, personalized therapeutic strategies.

paper.title: Enantioselective Neurotoxic Risk of Ethiprole Exposure to Honeybees: Prediction of Multidimensional Mechanisms.
paper.abstract: Limited research on the sublethal effects and mechanisms of chiral pesticides, particularly ethiprole, on honeybee neurobehavior at the enantiomeric level has obscured our understanding of the survival risks facing honeybees. We used transcriptomic sequencing, behavioral assay, correlation analysis, and molecular modeling to investigate the enantioselective neurotoxic risk of ethiprole on honeybees and predict potential molecular mechanisms. Our findings indicate that S-ethiprole poses a significant neurotoxicity hazard by markedly disrupting multiple signaling pathways and altering the expression of more genes, primarily by targeting the Rho subfamily of the small GTPase superfamily. This disruption likely accounts for the impairment of the gustatory response behavior in honeybees. Furthermore, Rac protein emerges as a potential molecular target through which S-ethiprole influences signal transduction in honeybees, correlating with decreased Snodgrassella abundance and the accumulation of N-benzoyl-N'-(2-chlorophenyl)thiourea induced by S-ethiprole. These results contribute to understanding the enantioselective neurotoxic risks and mechanisms of chiral ethiprole on honeybees.

paper.title: Decoupled Adult and Larval Host Preferences in Tephritid Fruit Flies with a Conserved Oviposition Attractant.
paper.abstract: Tephritid fruit flies exhibit considerable variability in host range, yet the chemosensory mechanisms underlying adult host selection and larval performance across species with contrasting dietary breadths remain unclear. Here, we investigated behavioral responses of adults and larvae of four species─Bactrocera dorsalis, B. correcta, Zeugodacus tau, and Z. cucurbitae─to seven fruit and vegetable cues. Adult preferences varied, with guava eliciting the strongest attraction in all species. Larval preferences were weaker and decoupled from adult choices. Comparative transcriptomics of guava-exposed antennae identified OBP19d as the most highly upregulated odorant-binding protein across species. RNAi knockdown of BdOBP19d in B. dorsalis reduced electrophysiological responses to guava volatiles and specifically abolished oviposition preference for 4-Ethylacetophenone. Molecular docking, electrophysiology, and behavioral assays collectively validated this interaction. These results reveal a conserved olfactory module for shared host attraction and identify 4-Ethylacetophenone as a candidate attractant for B. dorsalis females, with potential implications for pest management.

paper.abstract: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Within the Dlx-expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14, is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.

paper.title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity.
paper.abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)-localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

paper.title: Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions for reducing dental anxiety and improving behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients: a systematic review with GRADE assessment.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Dental anxiety affects an estimated 9%-20% of children and disproportionately impacts those with neurodevelopmental conditions. Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions, which intentionally modulate auditory, visual, tactile, olfactory, or proprioceptive input, have emerged as promising approaches for anxiety and behaviour management in paediatric dentistry, but no published review has applied formal GRADE certainty assessment across multiple sensory-based modalities. This review evaluated the effectiveness of sensory-based interventions for dental anxiety and behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients (≤18 years) and assessed certainty of evidence using GRADE.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: RCTs and controlled clinical trials involving paediatric participants (≤18 years) evaluating sensory-based interventions delivered during dental treatment or as pre-visit preparation, reporting dental anxiety, behavioural cooperation, or physiological stress, were eligible for GRADE assessment; eligible non-randomised, observational, pilot, feasibility, descriptive, and secondary studies were retained for narrative synthesis only. Studies of exclusively pharmacological or non-sensory cognitive-behavioural interventions were excluded.

METHODS: MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus, Embase, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 27 July 2026, supplemented by manual reference screening and Google Scholar searches. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment (RoB 2), and GRADE assessment. Given substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Of 2,002 records identified, 47 studies met inclusion criteria: 25 RCTs/controlled crossover trials contributing to GRADE assessment, and 22 non-randomised, pilot, observational, or secondary studies retained for narrative synthesis. Nine modalities were evaluated: sensory-adapted dental environments (SADE), audiovisual distraction/virtual reality (VR), music therapy, aromatherapy, weighted blankets, social stories, video modelling, visual pedagogy, and emerging sensory-based approaches. SADE, audiovisual distraction/VR, and music therapy showed the most consistent improvements in anxiety, cooperation, physiological stress, and pain, supported by moderate-certainty evidence for SADE and audiovisual distraction/VR; for music therapy, the direct paediatric primary-trial base is now a single GRADE-eligible RCT following reclassification of Chen and Hawkins (2021) to Tier 2 as a single-arm pilot without a concurrent comparator; certainty for music-therapy anxiety reduction is correspondingly rated low, supported by corroborating secondary meta-analyses. Certainty across modalities ranged from very low to moderate, limited by risk of bias, heterogeneity, inconsistent outcome measures, and imprecision. [Table: see text].

CONCLUSIONS: Sensory-based interventions show promising benefit for dental anxiety and behavioural cooperation in paediatric dental care, with the strongest (moderate-certainty) evidence for SADE and audiovisual distraction/VR, and low-to-moderate-certainty evidence for music therapy. Overall certainty remains low to moderate, supporting cautious, individualised clinical use rather than routine first-line implementation. Adequately powered trials with standardised outcomes, prospective registration, and GRADE-informed reporting are needed to strengthen the evidence base.Systematic Review Registration: identifier CRD420261456366.

paper.title: Neuroprogression of chronic stress-induced depression via longitudinal fMRI.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is increasingly viewed as a progressive neurobiological trajectory, yet the spatiotemporal transition from early mood dysregulation to chronic network failure, and its relation to disease-related functional decline, remains unclear. Using a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model, we aimed to map the longitudinal brain transformation from local spontaneous activity to global network dysfunction via multi-parametric MRI.

METHODS: Longitudinal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) was performed on a cohort of CUMS mice (n = 7) across three longitudinal time points: Day 0 (baseline), Day 5 CUMS, and Day 10 CUMS. We integrated four analytical approaches: fALFF, static functional connectivity, graph theory, and dFC/dALFF.

RESULTS: Depression progression followed a hierarchical spatiotemporal dissolution. fALFF revealed sequential breakdown of local hubs in caudoputamen, medial prefrontal cortex, and hippocampus, suggesting involvement of motor-motivational and executive deficits. sFC showed sensory-limbic uncoupling between caudoputamen and visual areas, and altered mPFC-AON connectivity and hippocampal prefrontal (HPF-PL) dysconnectivity, indicating limbic-olfactory loop disruption. Graph theory indicated preserved global node efficiency but widespread loss of node local efficiency and clustering. Dynamic analyses uncovered a shift from flexible network reconfiguration to dynamic rigidity.

CONCLUSION: Longitudinal CUMS exposure was associated with progressive alterations in functional network organization. The prefrontal olfactory dysconnectivity and onset of dynamic rigidity represent candidate multi-scale and longitudinal imaging features that warrant future validation.

paper.title: Substantial evidence against sex differences in bed nucleus of the stria terminalis volume in the human brain.
paper.abstract: "The bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) is a sexually dimorphic basal forebrain region" is a claim prevalent across rodent and human neuroscience research, arising from the observation that it is substantially larger in male versus female brains. Despite the pervasiveness of this claim, which may have implications for understanding sex differences in anxiety and substance use disorders, inspection of the literature reveals a complex and nuanced picture. Research on volumetric human BNST sex differences comes from a handful of mostly small-scale post-mortem studies and two MRI studies, between them reporting no, moderate, or very large differences. This indicates the need for a more detailed systematic investigation. Addressing this, we developed a novel 3T T1-weighted (T1w) manual segmentation protocol for the BNST, which was applied to sub-millimetre resolution T1w structural MRI data in 170 young human adults. Using a Bayesian modelling approach, taking into account existing data and accounting for total brain volume, age, and sibship, we find substantial evidence favouring no sex difference in total BNST volume. We recommend that researchers exercise caution when reporting evidence of BNST sexual dimorphism, particularly when translating findings from rodent models in which the BNST may play a different, olfaction-focused, role.

paper.title: Red Light Therapy and Mitochondrial Rejuvenation in Age-Related Disorders.
paper.abstract: Aging is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired ATP production, and a decline in tissue regenerative capacity, leading to the development of age-related diseases. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the effects of photobiomodulation (PBM) on mitochondrial function and age-related disorders. PBM using red and near-infrared light may enhance proper mitochondrial function by acting on cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) and other signaling pathways, including the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel, leading to increased ATP production, modulation of ROS signaling, and improved cellular homeostasis. We review in vitro, animal, and clinical studies investigating PBM in metabolic, neurodegenerative, hepatic, cardiovascular, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and skeletal muscle disorders associated with aging, as well as its application in the management of cancer therapy-related oral mucositis. Current studies demonstrate beneficial effects on glucose metabolism, cardiovascular function, neuronal function, lipid metabolism, liver function, muscle regeneration, and visual function in AMD, as well as the safety and efficacy of PBM in the management of cancer therapy-induced oral mucositis. The therapeutic effects of PBM appear to be dose-dependent and influenced by treatment parameters including wavelength, fluence, irradiance, and exposure protocol. Although photobiomodulation still lacks standardized treatment protocols and differences exist in the wavelengths used, dosage, and frequency among studies, it represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of age-related diseases.

paper.title: Microbial products trigger chemosensory dialogues through intestinal G protein-coupled receptors.
paper.abstract: Organismal reactions to changing environmental conditions require information relays that sense cues and elicit appropriate responses. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including olfactory receptors, comprise the largest receptor family that recognizes environmental cues, consisting of over 800 genes in the human genome. Here, by screening libraries of gut metabolites and natural products using a multiplexed GPCR reporter system, GPCR-seq, we reveal multiple intestinal chemosensory pathways. Among these, we determine that a cyclic fatty acid promotes serotonin production from enterochromaffin cells via olfactory receptor OR51E1. Two additional gut microbe-derived molecules, a β-carboline and 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), function as agonists for GPR35, a receptor linked to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The IBD-associated GPR35 risk variant, T108M, shows aberrant responses to 6-HNA, while Enterocloster bolteae, a species increased in IBD, generates high levels of 6-HNA. This approach provides an accelerated path to mapping critical chemosensory pathways and host physiological responses.

paper.title: PSMD12 is a novel potential biomarker for lung adenocarcinoma and associated with prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma patients.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to comprehensively evaluate the expression pattern of PSMD12 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and its impact on prognosis, and to explore its potential application value in the diagnosis and treatment of LUAD.

METHODS: This study employed bioinformatics analysis and molecular biology experiments to comprehensively investigate the expression pattern of the PSMD12 gene in LUAD and its association with LUAD patients' clinical features. First, we evaluated the differential expression of PSMD12 in 44 different tumor types and its relationship with the prognosis of LUAD patients. GO, KEGG, and GSEA were used to analyze the function of PSMD12. Secondly, TIMER was applied to evaluated the relationship between PSMD12 gene expression and immune infiltration characteristics in LUAD patients. Finally, RT-qPCR, CCK-8, clone formation assay, wound healing assay, and Transwell assay were used to verify the effects of knockdown PSMD12 expression on the proliferation, migration, and invasion abilities of LUAD cells.

RESULTS: Survival analysis results showed that high PSMD12 gene expression levels were significantly correlated with the poor prognosis of LUAD patients. The importance of PSMD12 in key metabolic pathways and disease processes such as neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, taste and olfactory transduction, and steroid hormone biosynthesis was revealed. Immune infiltration analysis results showed that PSMD12 expression was negatively correlated with M2 macrophages, revealing the potential role of PSMD12 in regulating the immune microenvironment of LUAD. In vitro experiments verified the functional role of the PSMD12 in LUAD cells, indicating that knockdown of PSMD12 weakened the proliferation, migration, and invasion abilities of LUAD A549 and H1299 cells.

CONCLUSIONS: High expression of PSMD12 may be closely related to poor prognosis in LUAD patients and promotes the malignant progression of LUAD by enhancing the proliferation, migration, and invasion of LUAD cells.

paper.title: Silencing RpadOrco disrupts host seeking, semiochemical avoidance and reproductive fitness in Rhopalosiphum padi.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The odorant receptor co-receptor (Orco) is an important component of the insect olfactory system. However, the biological functions of Orco in the bird cherry-oat aphid, Rhopalosiphum padi, remain unclear, particularly its roles in olfactory perception, host-plant selection and aphid fitness.

RESULTS: RpadOrco was predominantly expressed in the antennae. RNA interference-mediated knockdown of RpadOrco significantly reduced electroantennogram responses to 11 behaviorally relevant odorants, including plant volatiles, the repellent methyl salicylate (MeSA) and the alarm pheromone (E)-β-farnesene (EBF). In Y-tube olfactometer assays, RpadOrco-silenced aphids no longer showed significant orientation toward wheat and exhibited attenuated avoidance responses to MeSA and EBF. Silencing RpadOrco also increased the proportion of aphids that made no choice in the Y-tube olfactometer assays and significantly reduced body weight and fecundity in the F0 generation, without affecting survival. However, no significant changes were detected in developmental duration, longevity or life-table parameters in the F1 generation.

CONCLUSION: RpadOrco plays an important role in host-plant orientation, semiochemical perception and reproductive fitness in R. padi. Its simultaneous effects on olfactory behavior and fecundity identify RpadOrco as a potential molecular target for developing behavior-disrupting and RNAi-based approaches to cereal aphid management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

paper.title: Density-dependent olfactory responses of Ectropis obliqua to tea plant volatiles induced by Empoasca pirisuga.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tea plants (Camellia sinensis) are persistently threatened by multiple co-occurring herbivore pests. Empoasca pirisuga and Ectropis obliqua are two dominant species in tea plantations, and the alternation of their population dominance is driven by complex ecological mechanisms that remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize density-dependent olfactory responses of E. obliqua to herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) from tea plants infested by E. pirisuga under laboratory conditions.

METHODS: Headspace volatile profiles induced by six graded densities of E. pirisuga were identified and quantified via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) with solid-phase microextraction (SPME). Multivariate analyses (PERMANOVA and PCA) were used to assess global differences in volatile blends. Olfactory responses of virgin female E. obliqua adults to induced volatiles and to synthetic candidate compounds were assessed using a Y-tube olfactometer with clean air or hexane solvent as the reference control.

RESULTS: Infestation density significantly altered the composition and relative abundance of tea plant HIPV blends (PERMANOVA, P < 0.001). β-ocimene, methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and methyl salicylate (MeSA) were identified as the three major density-responsive components. E. obliqua exhibited a clear density-dependent valence shift in response to induced HIPVs relative to clean air: low-density infestation produced blends that significantly attracted E. obliqua, whereas high-density infestation elicited strong repellency. Synthetic compound bioassays confirmed that β-ocimene and MeJA function as individual attractants, while MeSA acts as an individual repellent for virgin female E. obliqua under laboratory conditions.

DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that density-dependent modulation of HIPV blends is associated with interspecific olfactory responses between E. pirisuga and E. obliqua under controlled laboratory conditions. This work provides a chemical basis for hypotheses regarding pest dominance alternation in tea agroecosystems, which require further field validation including oviposition, colonization and population-level assays.

paper.title: Hemorrhagic Papilledema in a Patient With End-Stage Renal Disease and Meningioma: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: Anterior cranial fossa meningioma can present with a constellation of symptoms that pose a diagnostic challenge, especially in patients with significant comorbidities like end-stage renal disease (ESRD). We report a case where the classic triad of visual loss, headache, and anosmia was initially complicated by the patient's renal background and systemic inflammation. A 53-year-old woman with ESRD and hypertension presented with a one-month history of progressive, non-correctable bilateral visual loss and a two-week history of headache. She also reported complete anosmia. Her medication regimen was comprehensive for her comorbidities. Uncorrected and corrected visual acuity was 6/10 OD and 7/10 OS. Funduscopy revealed bilateral optic disc edema with peripapillary hemorrhages. The Marcus Gunn test was negative. Systemic inflammation was evidenced by an elevated ESR (51 mm/h) and a positive CRP. Brain MRI confirmed the presence of a meningioma. Her blood pressure was controlled at 130/83 mmHg. The patient's presentation is a classic depiction of an anterior cranial fossa meningioma, likely originating from the olfactory groove or planum sphenoidale. The tumor explains the anosmia via direct nerve compression and the papilledema via obstruction of CSF pathways and elevated intracranial pressure. The controlled blood pressure and the specific nature of the triad helped exclude hypertensive emergency and uremic encephalopathy as primary causes. The elevated inflammatory markers, while raising initial suspicion for vasculitis or other inflammatory conditions, are also a known, though less common, associated finding with meningioma. This case underscores the critical importance of pursuing a central nervous system (CNS) etiology for neurological symptoms, even in medically complex patients. The triad of papilledema, headache, and anosmia is highly suggestive of an anterior cranial fossa mass lesion and warrants prompt neuroimaging. Systemic inflammation should not prematurely divert the diagnostic workup from considering primary CNS tumors.

paper.title: Kallmann syndrome revealed by primary amenorrhea: Phenotypic variability and diagnostic challenges-A report of three cases.
paper.abstract: Kallmann syndrome is a rare form of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with anosmia or hyposmia. We describe 3 female patients aged 17, 17, and 22 years who were evaluated for primary amenorrhea and reported lifelong anosmia. Hormonal assessment demonstrated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed bilateral olfactory bulb agenesis in 2 patients and unilateral agenesis with contralateral hypoplasia in one. The clinical presentations varied: 1 patient had complete secondary sexual development, another had a maternal history of anosmia and delayed puberty, and the third had incomplete pubertal development with a borderline low morning cortisol level. Genetic testing was not performed. The combined clinical, hormonal, and imaging findings were strongly supportive of Kallmann syndrome. Treatment was individualized according to pubertal stage. These cases emphasize the value of systematic olfactory assessment and dedicated evaluation of the olfactory bulbs and sulci on magnetic resonance imaging in females with primary amenorrhea.

paper.title: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-out of abnormal chemosensory jump 6 (acj6) gene impacts Helicoverpa armigera antennal lobe structure.
paper.abstract: The specificity of the olfactory system in the brain is determined not only by the expression of odorant receptor genes but also by the specific neural circuit assembly within the antennal lobe (AL). To investigate the developmental role of abnormal chemosensory jump 6 (acj6) in the moth Helicoverpa armigera, we generated Haacj6 mutants using CRISPR/Cas9 and examined the detailed structure of the AL based on immunostaining and three-dimensional reconstruction. The results showed that the AL in male Haacj6 mutants was markedly enlarged. In both sexes, the AL of Haacj6 mutants contained approximately 100 glomeruli, compared with about 75 glomeruli in wild-type. Glomerular volumes were also more heterogeneous in the mutants: the largest glomeruli were expanded, whereas the smallest were reduced, although the mean glomerular volume remained unchanged. These results demonstrate that the Haacj6 gene plays a critical role in normal AL development and that AL enlargement in the mutants arises primarily from the presence of additional glomeruli. These additional glomeruli likely reflect defects in olfactory receptor neuron axon wiring to AL projection neurons, or glial mediated glomerular boundary formation. These findings indicate that acj6 is an essential regulator of AL architecture and provide crucial insights into the molecular mechanisms governing neural circuits assembly in insects.

paper.title: Carotid body carcinoma in a French bulldog treated with toceranib phosphate.
paper.abstract: Carotid body tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms in dogs, and evidence-based treatment options for malignant or unresectable cases remain poorly defined. An 8-year-old castrated male French bulldog was presented with a large cervical mass accompanied by progressive respiratory distress, neurologic abnormalities, and exophthalmos. Computed tomography revealed multiple, highly vascularized cervical masses with extensive local invasion, including nasopharyngeal obstruction and intracranial extension. Partial surgical excision was undertaken for diagnostic purposes, and histopathologic examination confirmed carotid body carcinoma with intravascular invasion. Because of incomplete surgical resection and malignant features, targeted therapy was initiated. Based on in vitro chemosensitivity testing, toceranib phosphate was selected. Following treatment, clinical signs related to mass effect improved, nasopharyngeal obstruction was alleviated, and increased intratumoral necrosis was suspected on follow-up imaging. Adverse effects were mild and manageable. The dog remained clinically stable for ~5 mo after targeted therapy but was subsequently lost to follow-up. On a later follow-up via telephone, the owner reported that the dog had died 6 mo after initiation of targeted therapy. Key clinical message: This case suggests that toceranib may represent a potential therapeutic option for dogs with unresectable or incompletely resected carotid body carcinoma.

paper.title: Motor Cortex Disinhibition Is Dissociated from Clinical Motor Features in Parkinson's Disease: Longitudinal Evidence.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Parkinson's disease, motor dysfunction largely reflects dopamine-dependent pathophysiological alterations and compensatory mechanisms that progress over time and are partially reversible with dopaminergic treatment. Our recent cross-sectional observations suggest that disinhibition of the primary motor cortex-assessed with short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) using transcranial magnetic stimulation-does not correlate with clinical motor features, does not progress across disease stages, and instead correlates with olfactory dysfunction, a common prodromal and dopamine-independent feature.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to provide longitudinal evidence for or against the hypothesis that motor cortex disinhibition is dissociated from clinical motor features in Parkinson's disease.

METHODS: We compared SICI across three cohorts (total n = 95 patients): (1) baseline and 2-year follow-up (n = 43), with concurrent motor assessment and 18F-DOPA positron emission tomography (PET) imaging (n = 24); (2) before and after levodopa administration (n = 30); and (3) before and after focused ultrasound subthalamotomy (n = 22). We also included a pooled healthy control group (n = 75) from two previously published studies. Bayesian statistics was applied to formally assess evidence for the presence or the absence of an effect.

RESULTS: SICI was expectedly reduced, with very strong to extreme Bayesian evidence, in patients compared with control subjects. We found evidence that cortical disinhibition did not worsen with clinically evident disease progression confirmed with 18F-DOPA PET and did not improve following a clinically effective dose of levodopa or subthalamotomy. Moreover, changes in SICI did not correlate with changes in motor features across cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide longitudinal evidence that motor cortex disinhibition is largely dissociated from clinical motor features in Parkinson's disease. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

paper.title: The novel role of T2R14 antagonism, by LW129, on VEGF-induced lung endothelial neovascularisation processes in vitro.
paper.abstract: Pulmonary vascular remodelling, driven by dysregulated angiogenesis, is a hallmark of several cardiopulmonary diseases, yet the molecular pathways regulating endothelial responses remain incompletely understood. Bitter taste receptors (T2Rs), traditionally recognised as chemosensory receptors, have emerged as important modulators of vascular function. However, the contribution of T2Rs to pulmonary angiogenesis remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the role of T2R14 in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mediated angiogenic responses in human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs). Using the selective T2R14 antagonist LW129, we examined the effects of T2R14 inhibition on key endothelial angiogenic processes, including VEGF-induced proliferation, migration and capillary-like tube formation in vitro. Pharmacological antagonism of T2R14 significantly attenuated VEGF-driven endothelial proliferative, migratory and morphogenic responses, revealing a novel contribution of T2R14 signalling to pulmonary microvascular angiogenesis. Proteome Profiler analysis identified a range of molecular regulators of angiogenic processes which were dysregulated by LW129 and VEGF exposure, suggesting a potential role for CXCL16, endoglin, FGF-7, and VEGF-C. These findings identify T2R14 as a novel regulator of VEGF-dependent endothelial activation and suggest that targeting T2R14 signalling may represent a therapeutic strategy to limit pathological pulmonary vascular remodelling associated with aberrant angiogenesis.

paper.title: Evaluation of radiotherapy-related oral complications and functional outcomes in patients with oral cavity carcinoma.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Radiotherapy (RT), a major treatment modality for head and neck cancers, may cause oral complications such as mucositis, xerostomia, dysphagia, and taste dysfunction, negatively affecting patients' quality of life and treatment compliance. This study aimed to evaluate longitudinal changes in salivary flow and gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) volume and explore associations between RT-related oral complications and periodontal status, radiation dose, volumetric parameters, and tumor localization in patients with oral cavity cancer (OCC).

METHODS: Fifty-two patients with OCC who underwent surgery and were scheduled for RT were enrolled in this prospective study. Of these, 28 completed the T1 assessment and were included in the longitudinal and oral complication analyses. Clinical periodontal examinations and saliva and GCF sampling were performed at baseline (T0) and eight weeks after RT initiation (T1). RT-related oral complications were monitored during the study period. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between patients who completed and did not complete the T1 assessment to explore potential attrition-related differences. Statistical analyses included descriptive, comparative, and correlation analyses, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Among the 28 patients with paired measurements, GCF volumes (µL) were 50.80 ± 36.53 at T0 and 55.32 ± 36.31 at T1, while salivary flow rates (mL/min) were 0.34 ± 0.27 and 0.27 ± 0.26, respectively. Neither GCF volume (p = 0.655) nor salivary flow rate (p = 0.084) showed a statistically significant overall change. An exploratory analysis stratified by prescribed primary planning target volume (PTV) dose (62-64 Gy vs. 66-70 Gy) identified a significant time effect for salivary flow (p = 0.042), whereas no significant change was observed in GCF volume. Stratification by elective PTV dose (54-56 Gy vs. 58-60 Gy) revealed no significant longitudinal changes in GCF volume (p = 0.647) or salivary flow (p = 0.089). Among the 28 patients included in the oral complication analyses, mucositis was the most frequently observed complication (82.1%), predominantly Grade 1-2, followed by xerostomia (39.3%) and dysphagia (35.7%). No statistically significant differences were observed in the evaluated baseline characteristics between patients with and without T1 follow-up data (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Oral complications were frequently observed during RT in patients with OCC. Although an exploratory dose-stratified analysis identified a significant time effect for salivary flow, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited analytical sample, substantial loss to follow-up, incomplete complication data, and reliance on prescribed PTV doses rather than organ-at-risk dosimetry. Larger prospective studies with more complete follow-up and detailed dosimetric assessment are needed to clarify these associations.

paper.title: Navigating the diagnostic spectrum and challenges of rare sinonasal tumors: Lessons from a tertiary centre.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The sinonasal tract harbors a histopathologically diverse and uncommon group of neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges due to overlapping morphological features and nonspecific clinical presentations.

AIMS: This study aims to elucidate the clinicopathological and histopathological spectrum of rare sinonasal tumors seen at a tertiary care centre, with a specific focus on diagnostic pitfalls and the systematic approach necessary for accurate classification.

SETTINGS AND DESIGN: A retrospective, descriptive clinicopathological case series conducted at a high-volume tertiary care referral centre in London.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: All sinonasal tumor biopsies accessioned over one calendar year (November 2024 to October 2025) were reviewed. Non-malignant lesions and inverted papillomas were excluded. Thirty-two tumors, including rare lesions like sinonasal melanomas, angiosarcoma, olfactory neuroblastoma, sinonasal glomangiopericytoma (SNGP), adenoid cystic carcinoma, and rare subtypes of squamous cell carcinomas (SCC), were analyzed. Two unclassifiable neoplasms, despite extensive ancillary testing, were also included.

STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics were employed to summarize demographic, clinical, and pathological parameters.

RESULTS: These cases exemplified major diagnostic dilemmas, particularly in differentiating small round blue cell, spindle cell, and salivary gland-type tumors. A systematic, tiered immunohistochemistry (IHC) approach was instrumental in establishing definitive diagnoses in most cases. However, two tumors remained unclassifiable even after comprehensive IHC and molecular analysis, emphasizing the limitations of current diagnostic tools.

CONCLUSIONS: Rare sinonasal tumors remain a formidable diagnostic challenge due to their rarity and morphological overlap. Accurate diagnosis necessitates clinicopathological correlation, judicious use of IHC panels, and awareness of rare entities to prevent misclassification and ensure optimal patient management.

paper.title: Epistatic interactions in the evolution of Tasmanian devils and their transmissible cancer.
paper.abstract: Epistasis, the interaction among genetic loci whereby the effect of one variant depends on variation at other loci, shapes phenotypic variation and evolutionary trajectories across life. Cancer, a leading cause of death globally, provides a particularly compelling context for epistasis due to its clonal reproduction. Transmissible cancers, a rare subset of cancers capable of horizontal transmission between hosts, represent a unique evolutionary system in which tumor cells function as infectious agents. Considering the simultaneous maintenance of both within-host fitness and between-host transmissibility, many phenotypes in transmissible cancers and their hosts are likely governed by epistatic interactions. Yet the role of epistasis in the evolution of transmissible cancers remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigated epistatic interactions associated with host susceptibility to devil facial tumor disease 1 (DFT1), a species-specific transmissible cancer afflicting Tasmanian devils (Sarcophilus harrisii), using marginal epistasis tests applied to 312 matched devil-tumor paired genomes. We identified 50 candidate epistatic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in devils, with gene ontology enrichment for glutathione transferase activity, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis, and sensory perception of chemical stimuli, implicating oxidative stress response, metabolic reprogramming, and potentially olfactory-mediated disease avoidance in shaping host susceptibility. In contrast, only two significant SNPs were detected in DFT1, potentially suggesting a reduced epistatic contribution to tumor transmissibility compared with host susceptibility. Here, we have documented evidence of epistasis contributing to a disease-related trait in both devils and DFT1, highlighting the need to account for epistatic interactions in future studies of transmissible cancer evolution and host-pathogen dynamics more broadly.

paper.title: Lipid contribution to volatile formation in paper-wrapped Chinese bacon under different smoking temperatures and durations.
paper.abstract: This study explored the lipid contribution to volatile formation in paper-wrapped Chinese bacon under the influence of different smoking temperatures, alongside the dynamic changes in lipid profiles during the smoking process. Electronic nose and tongue analyses effectively distinguished the instrumental taste/odor pattern across different temperatures. Specifically, cold smoking (≤ 30 °C) significantly enhanced smoky aroma of paper-wrapped bacon by promoting the accumulation of alcohols, aldehydes, and ketones in the later stages, while warm smoking (45 ± 5 °C) effectively inhibited bitterness and astringency. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified 94 volatile compounds, with the cold-smoked group exhibiting a higher total volatile content than the warm-smoked group throughout the process. Among the 30 differential volatile compounds identified (VIP > 1), Strecker aldehydes and smoke-derived phenolics predominated in warm-smoked samples, whereas creamy ketones and terpenoids were enriched more in cold-smoked ones. Lipidomics detected 2862 lipid molecules, primarily including triglycerides, phospholipids, and sphingolipids. Linear mixed model analysis revealed significant main and interactive effects of smoking temperature and duration on the abundances of key lipids and volatile compounds (P < 0.05), with cold and warm smoking driving divergent temporal trajectories. Furthermore, three core volatile formation pathways were clarified, including glyceride, phospholipid, and sphingolipid metabolism, alongside smoke adsorption. These findings elucidate the molecular mechanisms of smoking temperature regulating the aroma development of paper-wrapped bacon, thus providing a theoretical basis for optimizing the processing technology of smoked meat products.

paper.title: An interpretable deep learning framework for revealing fine-grained spatial domains.
paper.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables gene expression profiling with preserved spatial context, yet accurate spatial domain delineation remains challenging. We present RIF, a robust and interpretable deep learning framework for fine-grained spatial domain identification. RIF leverages graph neural networks semi-supervised with pseudo-labels to preserve tissue structural integrity. It incorporates a dual-preprocessing ensemble strategy to improve model robustness and generalization. It further enables spatially variable gene detection through network interpretability. Across multiple sequencing platforms, RIF outperformed state-of-the-art comparison algorithms in spatial domain identification. In mouse brain tissue, RIF identified corresponding hippocampal subfields in the spatially separated dorsal and ventral regions and resolved the laminar organization of the olfactory bulb. In breast cancer, RIF-defined domains suggest suppressed T cell activity associated with hypoxic and oxidative microenvironments. In an invasive ductal carcinoma dataset of more than 720,000 cells, RIF-defined domains suggest an epithelial-mesenchymal transition gradient, including reduced hormone dependence and extracellular matrix remodeling.

paper.title: Multimodal sensory manipulation of first-year migrating passerines.
paper.abstract: How navigational cues are integrated during migration is still poorly understood, particularly in birds during their first migration. To test the hypothesis that first-year avian navigation is informed by multiple sensory systems (geomagnetic map information from magnetic particles and olfactory cues), we experimentally manipulated common redstarts Phoenicurus phoenicurus and blackcaps Sylvia atricapilla, undertaking their first autumn migration. We administered either a high-intensity magnetic pulse, or zinc sulphate anosmic treatment, or both. Migratory departure directions were determined in the natural environment using automated radiotelemetry. We predicted that if birds used these sensory systems with redundancy or in a hierarchical manner, single treatments would not change their migratory behaviour, however if birds simultaneously rely on multimodal sensory cues for navigation, the disruption of both senses will lead to incorrect or altered migratory orientation. The sample of birds which received the magnetic pulse only treatment departed in a seasonally appropriate direction equivalent to controls. This standard orientation was however significantly higher in concentration than the anosmic sample, suggesting anosmia disrupts normal migratory directed flight (and possibly vector navigation) in free-flying passerines on their first migration. The response to anosmia is surprising as olfaction has so far only been found to be involved in navigation of experienced birds during subsequent migrations. Furthermore, the sample treated with both magnetic and olfactory treatment oriented differently to other groups. Despite the low sample sizes, this study highlights that landscape level migratory behaviours and strategies are likely fundamental to the interpretation of studies on cue use in migratory animals.

paper.title: Vulnerability of the Brainstem-Cerebellar Respiratory Network in Extreme Prematurity.
paper.abstract: Survival of extremely preterm infants has significantly improved over the past decades, shifting critical stages of respiratory and brain development into the extrauterine environment. This transition exposes the vulnerable preterm infant to abrupt changes in oxygen tension, intermittent hypoxemia, inflammation, and oxidative stress, which contribute to maldevelopment of the structure and function of immature organs, including the brain and brainstem, with short- and long-term adverse consequences. This review examines how adverse intrauterine and extrauterine exposures during critical developmental periods in extremely low gestational age neonates (ELGANs) born <28 weeks of gestation disrupt the structure and function of key components of the central respiratory network, supporting epidemiological evidence that premature infants have a substantially increased risk of sudden unexpected infant death (SUID) during the first year of life and sleep disordered breathing across the lifespan. ELGANs are born during a period of rapid brainstem and cerebellar development, increasing the vulnerability of these regions to oxidative and inflammatory injury that can cause direct tissue damage and dysmaturation. The medullary serotonergic network and cerebellar fastigial nucleus regulate cardiorespiratory responses at rest and during progressive hypoxia and hypercapnia. We propose that adverse intrauterine and extrauterine exposures during critical developmental windows damage the macro- and microstructures, neurochemistry of these regions, impair protective respiratory responses, and mechanistically contribute to the two- to threefold higher risk of SUID in ELGANs than in term infants. We review fetal neuroprotective responses to hypoxia; the mechanisms and vulnerability of brain injury in ELGANs; the development and intrinsic hypoxic chemosensitivity of central respiratory control; and brainstem and cerebellar dysmaturation. Together, this framework provides a biological basis linking extreme prematurity to impaired ventilatory control, disordered breathing, and increased vulnerability to sudden death during infancy and beyond.

paper.title: Three-year real-world effectiveness of dupilumab in eosinophilic CRSwNP across upper and lower airways.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term real-world data on dupilumab in refractory eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) are limited, particularly regarding concurrent upper- and lower-airway control, inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) withdrawal in comorbid asthma, and olfactory recovery.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 104 patients with refractory CRSwNP who continued dupilumab for >3 years. Outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 3 months, and years 1-3. In patients with comorbid asthma, ICS exposure was quantified as the daily budesonide-equivalent dose and categorized according to a GINA-based inhaled maintenance step excluding biologics. Maintenance ICS withdrawal was defined as operational clinical remission with withdrawal of maintenance ICS-containing therapy. Predictors of persistent olfactory dysfunction were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses.

RESULTS: Upper airway outcomes, including nasal polyp score, CT score, and olfactory function, improved within 3 months and were maintained over 3 years. In patients with comorbid asthma, mean budesonide-equivalent ICS dose decreased from 625.1 to 241.6 μg/day at year 3, with step-down of inhaled maintenance therapy and increased maintenance ICS withdrawal. Persistent olfactory dysfunction occurred in 21.2% and was associated with age and disease duration (cut-offs 47.5 and 7.5 years), with an increased risk in the high-risk group (OR 6.2).

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term dupilumab provided sustained benefits across both the upper and lower airways and enabled progressive, ICS-sparing de-escalation of background asthma therapy, including maintenance ICS withdrawal. These findings suggest a shift toward remission off conventional therapy. Age and disease duration may enable risk stratification for persistent olfactory dysfunction and inform personalized management.

paper.title: Regio-specific glycan expression within the mammalian brain and tumors.
paper.abstract: The mammalian brain exhibits a complex glycan code that orchestrates neural connectivity, yet the spatial organization of functionally critical modifications of glycoproteins, such as fucosylation and sialylation, remains unclear. Using novel monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) designed for glycan detection, we mapped expression of glycan epitopes with unprecedented sensitivity, revealing non-overlapping expression patterns. Combined with targeted N-/O-glycan profiling, we found that expression of fucosylated and sialylated glycans occurs in anatomically distinct domains in both murine and human central nervous system (CNS). Key findings include fucosylated O-glycans marking brain endothelial cells, sialylated O-glycans decorating lecticans at the nodes of Ranvier, whereas the accessory olfactory bulb harbors unique fucosylated N-glycans. RNAseq and co-localization studies confirm regio-specific glycosyltransferase activity driving this partitioning. We also found that brain tumors are distinguished by upregulated expression of specific fucosylated/sialylated epitopes compared to normal tissue. The mAb-based approach uncovers regio-specific glycan expression with implications for neurodevelopment and cancer diagnostics.
