paper.title: Platformed Atmospheres: How Digital Platforms Reshape the Felt Experience of Family Life.
paper.abstract: This article develops the concept of platformed atmospheres to address how digital platforms reshape domestic life. Platformed atmospheres are defined as the multisensory and affective environments that emerge when platforms become infrastructural to family life, shaping not only what families communicate but the felt, sensory, and temporal conditions through which homes are inhabited. Drawing on interviews with twenty-one intergenerational families in the UK, the article shows that platforms operate as atmospheric infrastructures that structure how domestic spaces are sensed, occupied, and experienced. The analysis conceptualises platformed atmospheres as relational formations produced through encounters between bodies, devices, spaces, platforms, and data flows, negotiated within families yet unevenly experienced across generations and shaped by differences in age, embodiment, housing arrangements, and material resources. The article is grounded in the theory of atmospheres, drawing on feminist and sensory scholarship to foreground questions of inequality, materiality, and everyday experience, and apply these insights to the study of platform-saturated homes. In doing so, it asks what platform-saturated homes feel like, and for whom. Empirically, the analysis unfolds across three dimensions of platformed atmospheres. Spatially, platforms redistribute presence through features such as location tracking and video calling, reconfigure domestic boundaries like the closed bedroom door, and relocate sites of intimacy across households. Sensorially, platforms privilege vision and hearing while marginalising touch, taste, and smell, producing sensory substitution and generational distance in how care and closeness are felt. Temporally, platforms restructure family rhythms into polyrhythmic and often exhausting orders, through algorithmic time (autoplay, infinite scroll) and deferred co-presence (voice notes, asynchronous messaging) that stretch intimacy across misaligned tempos. The article concludes by showing how the concept of platformed atmospheres extends existing theories of atmosphere to networked, algorithmically mediated conditions, and extends theories of digital family life by foregrounding the pre-reflective, felt dimension underlying communication, monitoring, and care, before identifying directions for future research on digitally mediated inequality and everyday experience.

paper.title: Optic nerve hypoplasia and septo-optic-pituitary dysplasia.
paper.abstract: The presence of a small optic disc on funduscopy is prerequisite for the diagnosis of optic nerve hypoplasia (ONH). Visual acuity may be normal. However, amblyopia can occur in ONH. A relative afferent pupillary light defect indicates unilateral or asymmetrical ONH. Septo-optic-pituitary dysplasia (SOD) is diagnosed when ONH is associated with midline defects (e.g. hypopituitarism, small pituitary gland size, absent septum pellucidum, or abnormal corpus callosum). Olfactory bulbs/tracts agenesis or hypoplasia may occur with loss of smell. Pituitary function, neurological comorbidities (e.g. epilepsy, cerebral palsy), and psychiatric comorbidities (e.g. mood or anxiety disorders) should be evaluated regularly in patients with ONH/SOD. The risk of hypopituitarism continues until pubertal completion. Autopsy studies suggest that SOD is a clinical and not a neuropathological diagnosis. Children and especially infants/toddlers with SOD are at higher risk of acute hospital admissions and death than children without ONH/SOD. Respiratory tract illnesses are a common reason for their admission and is a frequent cause of their death. Healthcare professionals should be familiar with the comorbidities and complications associated with ONH/SOD, since they can be managed to reduce the mortality risk.

paper.title: Functional Response and Predation Potential of Arma custos (Fabricius) Against Tuta absoluta (Meyrick).
paper.abstract: The tomato leafminer, Tuta absoluta (Meyrick) (Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae), is a globally invasive pest causing severe economic losses in tomato production. We evaluated the predatory stink bug Arma custos (Fabricius) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) using functional-response assays, a predator-density experiment, behavioral observations, Y-tube olfactometer bioassays, and a greenhouse cage trial. Depletion-aware maximum-likelihood models supported a Type III response for adult females feeding on second-instar larvae, whereas Type II models were retained for fifth-instar nymphs and adults feeding on fourth-instar larvae. At an initial density of 40 larvae, females consumed 16.2 ± 0.2 second-instar or 17.4 ± 0.5 fourth-instar larvae within 24 h. With 40 fourth-instar larvae available per arena, increasing female density from one to five reduced per capita consumption from 17.40 ± 0.51 to 5.44 ± 0.04 larvae per day. The Hassell-Varley model provided the best fit (m = 0.725; 95% CI, 0.693-0.755). In greenhouse cages, releasing three females per cage reduced cumulative damaged leaves by 60.12% by day 15. No active larvae were detected in release cages at that time, compared with 11.33 ± 0.33 in controls. Females preferred infested over healthy tomato plants, whereas males showed no significant preference. These findings demonstrate that A. custos is a promising biological control agent for integrated pest management (IPM) of T. absoluta.

paper.title: Screening of terpenes and phenylpropanoids against Amblyomma sculptum nymphs: Non-spatial and spatial repellency.
paper.abstract: Repellents are important tools for preventing bites from arthropod vectors of pathogens, including the tick Amblyomma sculptum, a vector of the etiological agent of Brazilian Spotted Fever. Evidence from the scientific literature indicates that essential oils (EOs) and their constituent compounds, including terpenes and phenylpropanoids, have potential as tick repellents. Thus, the aim of this study was to evaluate the non-spatial (contact) and spatial (olfactory) repellent activity of botanical compounds (= natural compounds) commonly found in EOs against unfed A. sculptum nymphs, and to compare their repellent efficacy with that of DEET, the gold-standard arthropod repellent. Initially, Petri dish assays (contact, non-spatial repellency) were conducted using the following botanical compounds: (i) monoterpenes - carvone, citral, β-citronellol, linalool, p-cymene, α-pinene, and thymol; (ii) sesquiterpenes - α-bisabolol, caryophyllene, and nerolidol; and (iii) phenylpropanoids - cinnamyl acetate, trans-anethole, and (E)-cinnamaldehyde; at concentrations of 1% and 5% (w/v). DEET was tested at a concentration of 15%. All compounds were commercially obtained from Sigma-Aldrich. Subsequently, the compounds that showed the highest efficacy in the contact repellency assay (nerolidol and α-bisabolol: > 85%) were evaluated for olfactory (spatial) repellency using a Y-olfactometer. It was observed that, in the contact test, the monoterpenes at the 1% concentration did not exceed 80% of repellency, with linalool reaching the higher rate (69%). At the 5% concentration, thymol, citral, and β-citronellol showed over 80% of repellency, although none reached the established cutoff value (85% of repellency). Among the sesquiterpenes, caryophyllene exhibited the best repellency mean at 1% (70.7%) without statistical significance, while α-bisabolol (92.5%) and nerolidol (89.2%) surpassed 85% repellency at 5%, with significant results. Only α-bisabolol outperformed DEET (81%), and nerolidol was statistically equivalent. Among the phenylpropanoids, trans-anethole stood out at 1% (mean 76%), and cinnamyl acetate showed the best performance at 5% (mean 81.5%), but none reached 85%. In the spatial repellency test, DEET achieved 75.9% repellency; α-bisabolol showed no repellent effect, and nerolidol exhibited significant spatial repellency at both concentrations. Thus, it can be concluded that, among all the botanical compounds tested, α-bisabolol and, particularly, nerolidol were the most promising candidates for the development of tick bite repellents.

paper.title: Characterization and Behavioral Responses of Volatile Organic Compounds in Commercial Cockroach Baits.
paper.abstract: Cockroach baits are widely used due to their high efficacy and low environmental impact. However, a systematic understanding of the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that mediate attraction behavior in Blattella germanica, and their underlying mechanisms is still lacking. The behavioral and electrophysiological responses of B. germanica to 14 candidate VOCs were further evaluated using a Y-tube olfactometer and electroantennography (EAG). The results revealed significant differences in VOC composition among the tested baits, with aldehydes, acids, alcohols, and esters constituting the major components. This study identifies 2-methyl-3-buten-2-ol and hexanal as the key bioactive compounds responsible for attracting B. germanica in commercial baits. Their strong attractiveness at low concentrations indicates substantial practical application potential. These findings not only elucidate the chemical basis of the attractant activity of cockroach baits but also provide critical theoretical insights and technical support for optimizing existing bait formulations and developing novel, highly effective attractants.

paper.title: Constraints on oviposition learning: innate preference, cue integration and experience in a generalist fruit fly.
paper.abstract: Learning enables animals to adjust behavior in changing environments, yet it may be constrained by innate preferences and prior experience. We examined how these factors interact in oviposition site selection-a key fitness-related trait-in the highly polyphagous Mediterranean fruit fly, Ceratitis capitata. We addressed three questions: (i) whether learning depends on the strength of innate preferences; (ii) how visual and olfactory modalities contribute to learning; and (iii) whether egg laying is required to induce persistent preference changes. Using 3D-printed artificial fruits differing in color and olfactory cues, we showed that oviposition behavior was highly plastic but strongly constrained. Learning depended on innate preference strength: it was limited when innate preferences were strong, yet facilitated when they were weak. Both visual and olfactory cues supported learning, but only when the identity of both stimuli was consistent between conditioning and test phases. Importantly, the absence of egg-laying opportunity induced avoidance of associated sensory stimuli rather than attraction to them when oviposition opportunity is present, indicating that the outcome of an oviposition attempt strongly influences subsequent oviposition preferences. Our findings show that oviposition learning results from interactions among innate preferences, sensory integration, and associative reinforcement. These constraints have implications for understanding how generalist insects can use various host species throughout their life and how environments shape those decisions. In particular, it underlines that integrating experience-dependent changes in behavior is needed to improve behavioral pest management strategies.

paper.title: Differential attraction of Lygus hesperus (Hemiptera: Miridae) to host plants in the laboratory.
paper.abstract: Lygus hesperus Knight is a generalist pest of alfalfa, strawberry, cotton, and other crops in western North America. Female L. hesperus responded to host plant volatiles in both behavioral assays with the highest proportion of female L. hesperus moving upwind when exposed to Medicago sativa. When given a choice between M. sativa and each other species individually in Y-tube assays, female L. hesperus preferred M. sativa relative to Artemisia vulgaris, Fragaria ananassa, Hordeum jubatum, Plantago major, and Capsella bursa-pastoris. The information gathered in this study suggests a potential use of M. sativa as a trap for L. hesperus and points to specific plant volatiles to consider in the development of chemical lures for L. hesperus.

paper.title: Temporal dynamics of antennal responses encode plant stress and ecological relevance in Spodoptera littoralis moths.
paper.abstract: Polyphagous insects draw fitness-relevant information from complex plant odor blends, yet electroantennography (EAG) studies often emphasize response amplitude rather than temporal structure. We combined natural plant volatile stimuli, temporal EAG analysis, and machine-learning classification to examine the responses of male and female Spodoptera littoralis antennae to host/edible plants, non-hosts, and drought-stressed plants. Female responses showed stronger functional organization and higher classification performance for the above-mentioned categories, particularly for non-host plants, whereas males retained discrimination only under high-contrast stress conditions. These findings suggest that peripheral antennal dynamics preserve biologically relevant information about plant suitability and physiological state. More broadly, this framework offers a new approach for linking peripheral olfactory physiology with future electrophysiological and behavioral experiments.

paper.title: Trabecular meshwork cellular mis-trafficking of near-native and premature stop variants in glaucoma-relevant myocilin.
paper.abstract: Mutations in the myocilin olfactomedin (OLF) domain can cause vision loss in glaucoma by inducing protein misfolding in trabecular meshwork cells. However, not all mutations are causal for the disease. Here, we compare the cellular behaviors of two variants with uncertain contribution to glaucoma - namely, the missense variant A427T and premature stop variant Q368X - to those of wild type (WT) and disease variant Y437H. When expressed in an inducible immortalized trabecular meshwork cell line, inhibition of the proteasome rerouted WT myocilin from endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation to autophagy. By contrast, neither Y437H, A427T nor Q368X could be rerouted for degradation. Conversely, inhibition of autophagy caused accumulation of WT myocilin and did not promote clearance of any tested mutant myocilins. Although the Q368X OLF mutant is misfolded, the crystal structure of the A427T OLF mutant showed modest perturbations that were largely confined to the mutation site. Our study demonstrates that a full range of misfolded states of mutant myocilin can present challenges for protein quality control clearance pathways and expands the range of defects known to impair mutant myocilin clearance.

paper.title: Multichannel colorimetric sensor array enabled by microwave-rapidly synthesized Cu/Fe single-atom nanozymes for broad-spectrum pesticide screening.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The widespread and excessive use of pesticides poses significant risks to both human health and ecological integrity. Inspired by the mammalian olfactory cross-response mechanisms, colorimetric sensor arrays provide a rapid, cost-effective and visual platform for multi-residue pesticide monitoring.

RESULTS: Herein, we report a four-channel response array constructed from Cu-N-C and Fe-N-C single-atom nanozymes rapidly synthesized via microwave assistance. These nanozymes exhibit intrinsic laccase-like (LAC) and peroxidase-like (POD) dual enzymatic activities, which are differentially modulated by distinct pesticide classes to generate characteristic fingerprint-like responses. Integrating with linear discriminant analysis (LDA) for dimensionality reduction and visualization, this array successfully discriminates three major pesticide categories-sulfonylureas, organophosphates, and carbamates, comprising nine typical pesticides within the discrimination concentration range of 5-500 ng/mL, and further distinguishes pesticide mixtures of varying compositional ratios.

SIGNIFICANCE: Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) confirms the robust broad-spectrum classification capability of the system. The practical utility of this array is demonstrated through high-throughput screening of multi-pesticide residues in fruit samples. The synergistic integration of microwave-accelerated nanozyme synthesis and multichannel colorimetric sensing establishes a versatile and reliable paradigm for universal pesticide detection in complex matrices.
